# Java Edition protocol/Inventory

> Minecraft Java snapshot: `1.12.2`  
> Protocol version: `340`  
> Source: [Java Edition protocol/Inventory](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Inventory?oldid=2765344)

Minecraft displays the **player inventory** differently, according to how the window was opened. Ranges of slot indices vary in meaning between different “windows”. The [Open Window](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Open_Window "Protocol") packet indicates which window is being opened according to:

The slot number is calculated starting at 0, counting up through the window's unique slots, and then counting through the players inventory.

For all windows, the slot in the upper-left corner of the player's inventory is slot *n* where *n* is the number of unique slots, and slot number -999 is always used for clicking outside the window.

The number of unique slots in the window is sent in the [Open Window](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Open_Window "Protocol") ([Play](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Play "Protocol"), 0x2d, clientbound) packet for all storage windows (e.g. Chest, Dropper). For non-storage windows (the items get dropped when the window is closed, e.g. Workbench, Anvil), the received number of unique slots is always 0, but it can be looked up by the client from the window type.

The default inventory window, which is never explicitly opened by the server, has 10 unique slots.

Rectangular regions are always indexed starting with the upper-left corner and scanning across rows. If a window has a crafting region, the output slot is always slot 0 followed immediately by the input region.

Each window type is described in the following sections. All slot index ranges are inclusive and reflect the indices observed in the Minecraft protocol.

For the window properties (additional data in each window, e.g. smelting progress or enchantments), refer to the table in the [Window Property](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol#Window_Property "Protocol") packet.

Using -1 as slot index and as window id will set the cursor item (the stack dragged with the mouse).

## Player Inventory

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/thumb/Inventory-slots.png/300px-Inventory-slots.png?e5b77)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Inventory-slots.png)

Inventory slots

This is the inventory window that the player can always open, typically by pressing `E` since [Template:Minecraft Wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Template:Minecraft_Wiki?action=edit&redlink=1 "Template:Minecraft Wiki (page does not exist)"). Before, you had to press `I`.

| Slot range | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | crafting output |
| 1–4 | 2×2 crafting input (1 + x + 2 \* y) |
| 5–8 | armor (head, chest, legs, feet) |
| 9–35 | main inventory |
| 36–44 | hotbar |
| 45 | Offhand slot |

Note that this is different from inventory items stored in a player.dat file. This may help: <https://gist.github.com/459a1691c3dd751db160>

## Llama

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/thumb/Llama-strength5-slots.png/300px-Llama-strength5-slots.png?2af66)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Llama-strength5-slots.png)

Llama slots

The inventory that appears when a tamed llama is right-clicked and has a chest, or when the player's inventory is opened while riding a tamed llama. Depending on the value of the strength field, the number of chest rows may vary (max is 5, so 15 slots).

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/thumb/Ambox_warning_pn.png/32px-Ambox_warning_pn.png?b6e1c)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Ambox_warning_pn.png "File:Ambox warning pn.png")

There still is a saddle slot, even though it cannot be used and is invisible.

[![](https://minecraft.wiki/images/thumb/Ambox_warning_pn.png/32px-Ambox_warning_pn.png?b6e1c)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Ambox_warning_pn.png "File:Ambox warning pn.png")

Slot positions within the llama inventory vary - slot 2 may be at (1,0) or at (0,1) depending on the number of columns.

| Slot range | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | saddle |
| 1 | carpet |
| 2-(2+3\*Strength) | llama inventory |
| (2+3\*Strength)+1-(2+3\*Strength)+27 | player inventory |
| (2+3\*Strength)+28-(2+3\*Strength)+35 | hotbar |
